title: China-to-Timor-Leste Solar PV Inverter Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: EMC and Power Quality Evidence — IEC 62920 and IEC 61000 for Timor-Leste PV Projects
rows.target_requirement: For Timor-Leste PV inverter projects, EMC and power-quality evidence should be aligned to IEC 62920 and IEC 61000-series requirements. Timor-Leste market documents are not yet mature and largely project-driven, so installers and EPC teams should confirm report scope for each project before commissioning.
target_standards: IEC 62920 — Photovoltaic power generating systems — EMC requirements and test methods for power conversion equipment
IEC 61000 series — Electromagnetic compatibility and power quality
Timor-Leste ANE- and EDTL-level technical submission requirements for connected PV equipment
Project-specific grid and installation assumptions for 220/380 V 50 Hz
rows.china_equivalent: Chinese files usually rely on GB/T 37408-2021 and NB/T 32004 with CNAS EMC reports. These can support engineering review, but they are not automatic substitutes for Timor-Leste project documentation that is aligned with IEC 62920 and IEC 61000 expectations.
china_standards: GB/T 37408-2021 — 光伏并网逆变器技术要求
NB/T 32004 — 光伏并网逆变器技术规范
rows.gap: Gap: project-level evidence in Timor-Leste generally requires explicit IEC-clause mapping, especially where tropical climate drives installation layout, heat, and protection assumptions. Exporters should obtain EN- and Timor-Leste-relevant EMC mapping before treating Chinese domestic evidence as project-complete.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where project owners, ANE, or EDTL require EMC and power-quality evidence for grid connection
mandatory_status.cn: Chinese EMC evidence supports domestic acceptance but is not sufficient by itself for Timor-Leste project approval

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Prepare project-specific IEC 62920 and IEC 61000 evidence for Timor-Leste PV inverter deployments instead of relying only on domestic Chinese EMC reports. Ensure mapping coverage for coastal heat-humidity and installation layout assumptions.

rows.requirement: Timor-Leste Grid Connection — 220/380 V 50 Hz, IEC 62116 / IEC 61727, and Project-Specific Settings
rows.target_requirement: Solar PV inverter projects in Timor-Leste should be treated as ANE/EDTL project-review items with interconnection conditions, technical inspection, and commissioning acceptance. Timor-Leste's low-voltage context is 220/380 V at 50 Hz, which genuinely aligns with China's nominal value and frequency. This helps with basic configuration but does not replace local project-specific parameters such as frequency windows, protection settings, harmonics, metering, and communications.
target_standards: ANE/EDTL project-specific grid-connection and commissioning requirements in Timor-Leste
IEC 62116 — Utility-interconnected photovoltaic inverters — Test procedure of islanding prevention measures
IEC 61727 — Photovoltaic systems — Characteristics of the utility interface
rows.china_equivalent: Chinese PV inverter evidence commonly includes GB/T 19964-2024, NB/T 32004, and GB/T 37408-2021, and assumes 220/380 V 50 Hz systems. For Timor-Leste, this is a useful electrical baseline but must be complemented with ANE/EDTL project acceptance terms and local commissioning requirements.

NB/T 32004 — 光伏并网逆变器技术规范
GB/T 37408-2021 — 光伏并网逆变器技术要求
rows.gap: Gap: project files should add ANE/EDTL acceptance scope, commissioning tests, and local protection coordination. Nominal voltage and frequency alignment is advantageous, but not sufficient. For import planning, include heat/humidity assumptions from Timor-Leste deployment points and confirm whether grid commissioning is on public or private network.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for grid-connected PV projects where ANE/EDTL project acceptance applies; voltage/frequency match is supportive but not sufficient
mandatory_status.cn: Chinese documents are domestic support only

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] For Timor-Leste, 220/380 V 50 Hz grid alignment with China is a good starting point. Compliance is still decided by ANE/EDTL project acceptance requirements, especially protection coordination, reactive requirements, metering, communications, and commissioning readiness in each site.

rows.requirement: Safety and Timor-Leste Environmental Suitability — IEC 62109, ANE/EDTL Conformity, Heat and Humidity Derating
rows.target_requirement: Timor-Leste PV inverter documentation should follow domestic ANE/EDTL conformity expectations and IEC-aligned safety evidence. IEC 62109-1 and IEC 62109-2 are key for inverter safety and utility-interface behavior. Timor-Leste projects should additionally demonstrate climate suitability, including high-ambient operation limits, enclosure design for tropical conditions, thermal derating, and ventilation or cooling strategies.
target_standards: ANE/EDTL conformity route for regulated project-connected equipment
IEC 62109-1 — Safety of power converters for use in photovoltaic power systems — Part 1
IEC 62109-2 — Safety of power converters for use in photovoltaic power systems — Part 2
Project-level environmental assumptions: heat and humidity derating, enclosure and ventilation
rows.china_equivalent: Chinese documentation commonly uses GB/T 37408-2021, NB/T 32004, and GB/T 19964-2024, which are useful for baseline technical quality. For Timor-Leste readiness, these documents need explicit mapping to IEC 62109 clauses and local climate assumptions, especially for thermal rise and humidity control.

rows.gap: Gap: Chinese reports remain useful, but Timor-Leste projects require IEC 62109 mapping, heat/humidity derating curves for local deployment, and explicit documentation of moisture ingress and maintenance access. Add project-specific commissioning assumptions before export readiness decisions.

mandatory_status.target: Project-specific and commonly required where ANE/EDTL or project specifications call for IEC 62109 and environmental suitability evidence
mandatory_status.cn: Chinese documentation is preparatory; project-specific IEC mapping remains required

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Prepare IEC 62109-1/-2-aligned evidence with local climate assumptions for Timor-Leste projects; do not rely on Chinese reports alone. Include moisture ingress control, thermal derating, and commissioning assumptions in technical dossiers.
